Subject: Data retention & audit evidence for pilot

Hi Elena/Tom —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have the same scope for the pilot and the contract addendum: 

- Scope from discovery: NexaHealth will send production-ish traffic to a dedicated Redwood environment for the pilot (model inference only). Primary concerns you raised were PII handling, retention of request/response payloads, logging/audit evidence, and EU data residency for a subset of patients.
- Proposed retention approach for pilot: 1) PII fields stored 0 days (transient-only) where possible; 2) Non-PII telemetry/logs retained 7 days; 3) Derived artifacts (embeddings/indices) retained 90 days unless you request shorter; 4) Audit trail: redacted request ids + operational metadata retained 30 days for health checks and billing reconciliation.

Action items I can take this week:
- Attach a written retention proposal (see attached retention_proposal_v1.pdf) with explicit policy language we can drop into an addendum.
- Share the minimal set of audit artifacts we can provide (redacted sample logs and SOC2 link).
- Confirm how we can enforce EU-only residency for the pilot (hosted EU region vs Redwood Private).

Could you confirm: (A) whether your legal/procurement team needs a 0-retention certification or a contractual addendum, and (B) whether procurement should be looped in for a redline now or after we send the proposal?

If it helps, I can set up a short call with Ben (engineering) and Marissa (solutions) to walk through the technical controls and what evidence we can produce next week.

Thanks —

Hi Karthik —

Appreciate the clear recap. A couple clarifications from our side before we loop legal/procurement: 

1) PII 0-retention: when you say "transient-only", can you confirm that request/response payloads containing patient identifiers will never be persisted to disk, and that KV caches are not written to durable storage? We need a short technical statement we can include in the addendum.
2) Shortened logs: 7 days for non-PII seems reasonable, but we need the exact list of fields that are considered "non-PII telemetry" (request metadata only? request_id? hashed user ids?).
3) Data residency: we need EU-only residency for EU patient traffic; confirm whether hosted EU region is sufficient or whether you require Redwood Private for guaranteed EU physical storage. Also let us know the expected lead time and any cost delta.
4) Evidence: procurement will want a redacted sample audit log, SOC2 report, and a short statement on encryption at rest/in transit.

I'm attaching our security questionnaire with a few follow-ups (NexaHealth_security_questions.docx). Procurement (Maya) is included for contract timing.

We'd like to schedule a 30-minute follow-up (technical + procurement) next week. We prefer Tuesday or Wednesday morning PST.

Best,

elena@nexahealth.io

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@nexahealth.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention & audit evidence for pilot

Elena —

Thanks for the detailed questions. I'm Ben (engineering, infra). Below are concrete answers and two configuration options we commonly offer for pilots + enterprise addenda.

Short answers: yes, we can enforce per-tenant retention policies and support transient-only (0 days) for request/response payloads, with caveats spelled out below. EU residency is supported via our EU-hosted region for hosted customers (we pin compute & storage to eu-west-1). For higher compliance or air-gapped setups we also offer Redwood Private (on-prem/VPC).

Technical notes:
- Transient-only mode: request/response payloads are kept in-memory for the inference lifecycle and flushed from KV/cache; nothing is written to durable blob storage. We do keep short-lived operational telemetry (request_id, outcome, processing latency) in a separate encrypted telemetry stream that can be configured to 0/7/30 days.
- KV cache behavior: for models with large KV caches we can enable a policy to avoid durable checkpointing; default durable checkpoints are off for tenants opting into transient-only.
- Logging schema: we classify fields as PII (full name, email, SSN, MRN, patient identifiers) vs. non-PII (request_id, model_version, latency_ms, error_code). I will attach a redacted sample log and a short SOC2 pointer.

Two recommended options for the pilot (pick one):
A) Hardened transient mode (max privacy): PII fields 0 days; non-PII telemetry retained 7 days; derived artifacts disabled. Minimal telemetry for health (redacted request_id + status) retained 7 days.
B) Split retention (balance for observability): PII fields 0 days; non-PII telemetry 7 days; derived artifacts (embeddings) retained 90 days but encrypted and access-controlled. We can add a data-handling addendum specifying who can access derived artifacts, and automated purging after 90 days.

Evidence we can provide:
- redwood_sotc_summary.pdf (short SOC2 orientation and controls)
- redwood_audit_sample.log (redacted, shows the fields we can export)
- Standard encryption-at-rest/in-transit statement and certificate references.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm which option (A or B) you prefer for the pilot.
2) We prepare a short addendum and a proposed contract redline.
3) Tech deep-dive call (Ben + Marissa + Karthik) to walk through the sample logs and residency plan.

I can be available Tuesday 2026-03-09 09:00-11:00 PST or Wednesday 2026-03-10 08:00-12:00 PST — let me know what works.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Staff Engineer, Inference Platform | Redwood Inference

Karthik/Ben —

Thanks — we discussed internally and want to proceed with option B (split retention) for the pilot, with the following constraints to be captured in an addendum: 
- Explicit statement that PII fields are not persisted (0 days) and are not included in any durable backups.
- Derived artifacts retained 90 days, encrypted, and limited to named Redwood service accounts only.
- EU patient traffic must remain in EU region; please include the region pinning statement and expected lead time/cost in the addendum.
- We need the redacted audit sample and SOC2 pointer attached in the formal package.

Please prepare a draft retention addendum and a redline-ready contract for our legal/procurement; I attached a template with our standard wording for retention addenda (NexaHealth_retention_addendum_template.docx). Procurement (Maya) will coordinate the contract timeline — Maya, can you propose the window for review?

Prefer to schedule the technical + procurement call next Wednesday 2026-03-10 09:00 PST if that works for your team.

Best regards,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Product Security | NexaHealth
